A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PESO research, with matching authors, core method and original experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite reformatting and substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments on three Amazon categories, including baseline comparisons, regularizer ablations and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds user-group, distribution-shift, forgetting, additional-baseline, LC-REC and Yelp results.

M1.justification: Both versions use a single inherited LoRA adapter with cross-entropy and proximal regularization toward its previous frozen state. v2 specifies separate A/B parameter groups and expands the autoregressive likelihood description, but does not establish a changed algorithm. The four-token item representation and prompt already appear in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates three Amazon product categories under chronological and pseudo user-disjoint settings. v2 retains these and adds Yelp location/check-in recommendation, extending evaluation beyond e-commerce. Table 3 also separately evaluates dormant returning users and newly arriving users, broadening the populations explicitly examined.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds direct Instruments comparisons against O-LoRA, AM-LoRA, LSAT and LSAT with parameter inheritance. Existing cumulative-adapter and traditional baselines remain. Table 8 separately adds full-parameter fine-tuning and cumulative-data retraining comparisons against Single Evolving LoRA; that table does not include PESO.

E3.justification: v2 adds LC-REC backbone evaluation, final-model user-group tests, logistic-regression/AUC drift measurement, past-block forgetting evaluation and new training-paradigm controls. Appendix C.2 also changes the stated pretraining learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0002 while retaining Figure 4. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The original regularizer and hyperparameter analyses remain. v2 adds direct stability/plasticity probes using dormant versus new users, quantified temporal distribution shift, explicit forgetting measurements on previous blocks and robustness testing with LC-REC. These substantially extend the evidence examining PESO's behavior beyond aggregate recommendation accuracy.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental variability estimates. The added tables continue reporting point estimates; averaging over stages or recommendation metrics does not establish repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 scores and reported gains are unchanged, as are the original plotted results. New Tables 3 and 7–12 add substantial results. For example, Yelp NDCG@5 is 0.0199 for PESO versus 0.0190 for Single Evolving LoRA. LC-REC Hit@5 instead favors SD-LoRA, 0.0185 versus PESO's 0.0179. These are additional evaluations, not improvements to the original scores.

T1.justification: The central propositions, assumptions and proof arguments remain. v2 corrects dimensionally inconsistent subspace expressions in Appendix B.1, including theta0+Uv and the tangent-feature gradient projection. It also introduces the AUC-based drift-score definition and explicit storage-complexity reasoning. The new Appendix B.3 primarily supplies intuition for the existing corollary.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: recommendation requires a distinctive stability/plasticity balance, PESO supplies proximal single-adapter adaptation with direction-wise theoretical guidance, and it outperforms single and cumulative LoRA baselines. Additional evidence and future directions do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets intermediate-block forgetting as benign adaptation, explains retraining's weakness through dilution of recent preferences, and attributes full-parameter fine-tuning difficulties to insufficient structural regularization. It also interprets Yelp results as robustness to limited semantic information and discusses prompt-retrieval overhead. These substantially broaden mechanism and applicability arguments.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/documentation repository link, specifies separate A/B groups for attention and MLP modules, revises the documented base learning rate and explains adapter-storage and forward-pass requirements. Repository contents are not established by the PDFs, and the reproducibility statement still retains its future-release wording.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited literature and positioning through O-LoRA, AM-LoRA, LSAT, LC-REC and prompt-tuning comparisons. New Appendices E–F discuss prompt pools and connect PESO to broader temporal adaptation, agents and memory research. This extends research positioning beyond the original vision-adapter and continual-recommendation discussion.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section order remain. v2 clarifies data construction, parameter grouping and proof exposition, adds an intuitive appendix subsection, expands the research-question list and updates publication/contact text. The original prompt and LLM-use appendices move from D/E to G/H.

P2.justification: Document-wide typography and spacing changes, revised display placement and seven additional tables substantially expand the visual presentation. The new tables are v2 Tables 3 and 7–12. Figures 1–4 retain their image content, while the original dataset and traditional-comparison tables persist under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through direct user-group and forgetting analyses, relevant additional baselines, and evaluations beyond the original datasets and backbone. These address important gaps in evidence for the stability/plasticity and generality claims. Technical clarifications and reported code access also help. The gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: uncertainty and experimental details remain underreported, and some new superiority wording exceeds the evidence, notably LC-REC Hit@5 in Table 10.
